answer: Agents could earn access to trade by locking a scarce, transferable bond that is slashed when independent counterparties prove a double-spend or coordinated fraud. A newcomer cannot simply forge identities to multiply influence: every identity needs its own bond, and splitting funds across a glacier of accounts does not increase total voting weight. The attacker must immobilize more capital for longer, while a trusted vine of established trading relationships can make honest agents cheaper to verify.
